newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Kampo aims to use currency forwards soon.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Kampo aims to use currency forwards soon.

text.p: Japan's Postal Life Insurance Bureau (Kampo) is planning to use currency forward transactions soon to hedge its holdings of foreign currency-denominated bonds, a Kampo official said on Wednesday.
Kampo is one of the world's biggest investors, holding a total 95.56 trillion yen worth of funds as of the end of October.
"We're in the final stages of preparation so we can carry them (currency forwards) out soon," the official told Reuters.
He said the transactions would basically involve selling against the yen, in a forward trade, the foreign currency in which the bond is denominated.

Kampo held a total 3.52 trillion yen worth of foreign bonds, including Euroyen issues, as of the end of October, but is only allowed to carry out forward transactions to hedge for bonds it purchased since May 1995.
The official declined to disclose the amount of fresh investments it has made since May 1995 as that would invite speculation and affect the market.
Kampo has been able to use forward transactions from May 1995 following the revision of a law, but has not done so yet.
"But we still have not decided when to actually make the forward transactions," the official said.
Kampo is planning to consult two investment advisory firms about carrying out the forward transactions, the official added.
